about.metaDescription: Learn about chatflow-agent, the lightweight async multi-agent Python framework created by Gustavo Baranda, its design principles, and its open source community.
about.title: About chatflow-agent
about.subtitle: A lightweight, asynchronous Python multi-agent framework designed for building conversational workflows with native handoffs and multi-channel connectivity.
about.originP1: chatflow-agent was created to solve a practical need in conversational AI development: connecting language models with real applications and communication channels without introducing unnecessarily complex architectures.
about.originP2: The project embraces Python's simplicity, modularity, and flexibility, giving developers the building blocks to create conversational agents and integrate them into their own applications while staying in control of their architecture. As an open-source effort, it evolves alongside its community to make conversational AI solutions accessible, extensible, and maintainable.
about.p1Desc: Built on standard Python asyncio so your conversational flows stay responsive and fit cleanly into modern async applications.
about.p2Desc: Delegate conversations between specialized agents while preserving message history and session context.
about.p3Desc: Built-in support for WhatsApp, Telegram, and interactive CLI, plus integration guides for custom webhooks. See the technical documentation for deployment and security recommendations.
about.p4Desc: Maintain conversation history and state across turns with in-memory or SQLite storage. For multi-process or distributed setups, consult the concurrency guide in the documentation.
about.creatorBio: Architect and lead maintainer of chatflow-agent. Designed the core async multi-agent runtime, native handoff mechanisms, and channel adapters to make robust conversational AI accessible to developers worldwide.
about.communityDescription: chatflow-agent thrives thanks to contributions from the global open-source community. Developers, translators, testers, and users worldwide help improve the framework with every release.
about.closingTitle: Ready to Build Conversational Multi-Agent Systems?
about.closingSubtitle: Explore our comprehensive documentation or join discussions with the developer community on GitHub.

home.heroTitle: Build Chatflows and Contextual Multi-Agent Systems in Python
home.heroSubtitle: Connect language models with your tools, delegate specialized tasks across agents, and keep conversation state consistent across real messaging channels.
home.chatflowConcepts: How a chatflow works in Python
home.installSubtitle: Install the package from PyPI and run your first conversational agent in just a few lines of Python.
home.docsDiscoverySubtitle: Practical guides, architectural overviews, and verified Python examples for every stage of your conversational workflow.
home.docCard1Desc: Set up your Python virtual environment, install chatflow-agent, and configure provider credentials.
home.docCard2Desc: Architect specialized agents, configure runner lifecycle, and delegate conversation turns deterministically.
home.docCard3Desc: Build custom FastAPI endpoints, verify incoming WhatsApp HMAC signatures, and connect real-time channels.
home.featuresSubtitle: Modular building blocks to design, test, and integrate multi-agent workflows while keeping full control of your Python architecture.
home.featHandoffsDesc: Delegate conversations between specialized agents while preserving message history and shared session context.
home.featChannelsDesc: Built-in channels for WhatsApp (with HMAC signature verification), Telegram, and interactive CLI, plus patterns for custom HTTP webhooks.
home.featModelsDesc: Works out of the box with Google Gemini, Gemma, OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, and xAI Grok with unified configuration.
home.featMemoryDesc: Persist conversation history and session metadata with SQLite or in-memory stores, with transactional turn rollback when errors or timeouts occur.
home.featAsyncDesc: Built natively on Python asyncio to handle concurrent messaging traffic and asynchronous tool calls.
home.featToolsDesc: Equip agents with custom Python functions, automatic parameter schemas, and runtime argument validation.
home.communityTeaserDesc: chatflow-agent is an open-source project released under the MIT License, created and led by Gustavo Baranda with contributions from developers worldwide.
home.learnMoreAbout: Learn more about the project & maintainer

notFound.title: Conversation flow reached an unmapped route
notFound.description: The agent attempted a context handoff, but this path does not exist in the session graph. It may have been moved, renamed, or is currently under active development.

error.title: Conversation flow encountered an unexpected error
error.description: An unexpected exception halted processing in this route segment. The error boundary contained the failure and no sensitive information was exposed.

community.subtitle: An open source ecosystem built by and for developers creating conversational AI agents, tools, and multi-channel workflows in Python.
community.repoCardDesc: Explore the official Python SDK source code, star the project, browse commit history, and follow ongoing development.
community.issuesCardDesc: Encountered a bug or unexpected behavior in the SDK? Submit an issue with a reproducible example and environment details.

community.howToContributeSubtitle: We welcome contributions of all kinds — code, documentation, bug reports, and feedback. Here is how to get started:
community.step1Desc: Fork the official repository on GitHub and clone your fork locally to begin development.
community.step2Desc: Create a virtual environment with Python >= 3.10 and install the package with development dependencies using pip.
community.step3Desc: Write clear, typed async Python code, add unit tests for your changes, and run the test suite locally before opening a PR.
community.step4Desc: Open a descriptive Pull Request referencing any related issues and following Conventional Commits format.
community.guidelinesNoticeDesc: chatflow-agent is an open source project distributed under the MIT License and led by Gustavo Baranda. All collaboration, issue tracking, and roadmap discussions take place transparently on GitHub.
